cases.name: grafana_time_projection
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT UNIX_TIMESTAMP(ts) AS time_sec, value FROM telemetry WHERE ts BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) ORDER BY ts
cases.rationale: A timestamp projection without a fixed grouping cadence is safe only for whole-object caching.

cases.name: grafana_time_epoch_projection
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT UNIX_TIMESTAMP(ts) AS time_sec, SUM(value) AS total FROM telemetry WHERE tenant_id = 42 AND ts BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts
cases.rationale: The epoch projection does not establish reusable complete buckets.

cases.name: grafana_time_filter_between
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(ts)/(300) AS SIGNED)*300 AS SIGNED) AS time, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM telemetry WHERE ts BETWEEN FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: Grafana's inclusive BETWEEN upper bound may select a partial final bucket, so DPC fails closed to OPC.

cases.name: grafana_time_from_to_fixed_interval
cases.query_origin: Grafana macros composed into a half-open predicate
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(ts)/(60) AS SIGNED)*60 AS SIGNED) AS time, AVG(value) AS mean_value FROM telemetry WHERE site = 'denver' AND ts >= FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND ts < FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: A fixed cadence with an inclusive lower and exclusive upper raw-time range is DPC-safe.

cases.name: grafana_time_group_interval_variable
cases.query_origin: Grafana $__interval expanded using the corpus 1m minimum
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(ts)/(60) AS SIGNED)*60 AS SIGNED) AS bucket, MAX(value) AS peak FROM telemetry WHERE ts >= FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND ts < FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY bucket
cases.rationale: After $__interval becomes the documented 1m literal, the query has a deterministic DPC cadence.

cases.name: grafana_unix_epoch_filter
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(epoch_seconds/(300) AS SIGNED)*300 AS SIGNED) AS time, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM telemetry WHERE epoch_seconds > 1785542400 AND epoch_seconds < 1785628800 GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: Grafana's strict lower comparison omits the first boundary and is not a reusable half-open DPC range.

cases.name: grafana_unix_epoch_from_to
cases.query_origin: Grafana epoch macros composed into a half-open predicate
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(epoch_seconds/(300) AS SIGNED)*300 AS SIGNED) AS time, SUM(requests) AS requests FROM service_rollups WHERE region = 'us-west' AND epoch_seconds >= 1785542400 AND epoch_seconds < 1785628800 GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: Epoch-second bounds and a fixed five-minute cadence are DPC-safe when expressed half-open.

cases.name: grafana_unix_epoch_group_manual_alias
cases.query_origin: Grafana grouping macro with caller-provided alias
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(epoch_seconds/(300) AS SIGNED)*300 AS SIGNED) AS bucket, COUNT(*) AS events FROM service_events WHERE epoch_seconds >= 1785542400 AND epoch_seconds < 1785628800 GROUP BY bucket ORDER BY bucket
cases.rationale: The non-alias macro is DPC-safe when the query supplies a stable output alias.

cases.name: native_timestamp_half_open
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(recorded_at)/(900) AS SIGNED)*900 AS SIGNED) AS time, datacenter, AVG(cpu_percent) AS cpu FROM host_metrics WHERE environment = 'production' AND recorded_at >= FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND recorded_at < FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) GROUP BY time, datacenter ORDER BY time, datacenter
cases.rationale: A realistic filtered and dimensioned TIMESTAMP aggregation retains complete-bucket DPC semantics.

cases.name: epoch_nanoseconds_half_open
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(observed_ns/(300000000000) AS SIGNED)*300000000000 AS SIGNED) AS time, sensor_type, MAX(reading) AS peak FROM sensor_events WHERE customer_id = 17 AND observed_ns >= 1785542400000000000 AND observed_ns < 1785628800000000000 GROUP BY time, sensor_type ORDER BY time, sensor_type
cases.rationale: Nanosecond integer storage is DPC-safe when cadence and half-open bounds use the same unit.

cases.name: epoch_between_is_opc
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT CAST(CAST(epoch_seconds/(300) AS SIGNED)*300 AS SIGNED) AS time, COUNT(*) AS samples FROM telemetry WHERE epoch_seconds BETWEEN 1785542400 AND 1785628800 GROUP BY time ORDER BY time
cases.rationale: Inclusive BETWEEN remains OPC because the upper boundary can expose a partial final bucket.

cases.name: floor_qualified_zero_phase
cases.query_origin: Production query using explicit FLOOR grouping
cases.expanded_sql: SELECT FLOOR(UNIX_TIMESTAMP(m.`when`) / 300) * 300 AS bucket, m.cab_type AS metric, COUNT(*) AS trips, AVG(m.fare) AS mean_fare FROM `analytics`.`metrics` AS m WHERE m.`when` >= FROM_UNIXTIME(1785542400) AND m.`when` < FROM_UNIXTIME(1785628800) GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
cases.rationale: Initial FLOOR support is limited to a positive equal literal divisor/multiplier and therefore has a compile-time cadence and Unix-epoch-zero phase.
